title.narrative: Output 8.2. Increased capacity of Member States to improve governance and sustainability of social protection systems

description.narrative: The Royal Government of Cambodia (RGC) on 8th August 2022 established the Social Security Regulator (SSR) via the Sub Decree on Social Security Regulation under the Non-Banking Financial Service Act to improve oversight of the social security system and all social security operations to ensure efficiency, effectiveness, transparency, accountability and financial sustainability. The ILO supported the drafting of the Sub-Decree Social Security Regulation through direct consultations and provided technical inputs into the Sub-Decree. In addition, the ILO supported the capacity building of the Social Security Regulator through technical assistance on the Guidelines on Social Security Fund Investment and Social Security Risk Management Framework to support the SSR in implementing its mandate listed in the sub-decree.

description.narrative: The Royal Government of Cambodia (RGC) promulgated the Sub-Decree on Conditions, Formalities and Procedures for Implementing the Voluntary Social Security Scheme on Healthcare on 28 August 2023. This Sub-Decree provides the legal basis for the creation of a Voluntary Social Security Scheme on Healthcare to cover self-employed individuals and dependents of NSSF members including their spouses and children under the age of 18. The scheme was operational from 1st November 2023 and social security coverage is plausible for an estimated 2.9 million self-employed persons, and 5.7 million children, albeit voluntarily. With the financial support of the EU and UN, ILO has provided technical support to the RGC on the conceptualization, evidence gathering, advocacy, and facilitation of social dialogue, design, and drafting of the policy. This includes defining the context and the needs, reviewing the National Health Insurance, providing technical support towards the definition of dependents, costing of the scheme and the contribution rates, and facilitating social dialogue between the Government and social partners. ILO's technical inputs and recommendations were largely taken on board with the exception of the voluntary nature of the scheme. The RGC decided to start with a voluntary scheme before transitioning to a mandatory scheme.
